objective.statement: Write rests in a bar so that every beat can be seen.
successCriteria: I give each beat its own rest.
I know a minim rest may fill the first or last two beats of a 4/4 bar.
I can complete a bar that contains rests.

explanation.text: Rests need grouping just like notes. The simple rule is that every beat gets its own rest, so the beats stay visible.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4: a crotchet, two crotchet rests and a crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, crotchet rest, crotchet rest, crotchet.

explanation.caption: Beats two and three are silent, so each gets its own crotchet rest.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4 where one minim rest covers beats two and three.

explanation.caption: A minim rest across beats 2 and 3 hides the half-way point of the bar, so avoid it.

explanation.text: In 4/4 you may use a minim rest to fill beats one and two together, or beats three and four together. That keeps the half-bar clear.
If you are unsure, use one crotchet rest for each silent beat.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 4/4. The first has a minim rest then two crotchets. The second has a crotchet, a crotchet rest and a minim.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: minim rest, crotchet, crotchet. Bar 2: crotchet, crotchet rest, minim.

steps: Play all and count. In bar one, beats one and two are silent.
In bar two, beat two is a single silent beat.
Each rest lines up with the beat, so the pattern is easy to follow.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two bars of 4/4 with rests in clear places: a minim rest on beats one and two, and a crotchet rest on beat two.

mistakes.bar-overfull: This bar holds more beats than the time signature allows. Count the beats again and remove the extra.
mistakes.bar-underfull: There's still room in this bar. Count how many beats are missing.
mistakes.grouping-obscures-beat: The beats add up, but it's hard to see where each beat starts. Regroup the notes so every beat is visible.
mistakes.unnecessary-tie: You can write those tied notes as a single note (or a dotted note). That's easier to read.
mistakes.rest-grouping: Each silent beat (or part-beat) normally gets its own rest. Split the silence along the beats.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Check the beat total first, then how the notes are grouped.
